summary: The patch adds hir/abap/format.go with a small lexer and an indentation state machine. It replaces the old `wrap` with `Format` for every emitted file and routes all tsfront driver classes and reports through it. All tests pass. I generated the full lexer pipeline (71 files, about 25k statements) and checked it against @abaplint/core's own Indent.getExpectedIndents: there were 0 mismatches, every line was at most 255 bytes, and both Format and indent were exact fixed points on the output. Hand-made edge cases also came out right: literals and templates with escaped delimiters, comments, report events, forms, DEFERRED/LOAD class declarations, runtime GET statements, SELECT/ENDSELECT, CATCH SYSTEM-EXCEPTIONS and wrapping between statements.

findings.claim: formatABAP silently discards Format errors and returns the unformatted source. If a driver ever contains an unbreakable line longer than 255 bytes, it is emitted unindented and over-long without any diagnostic, so the driver-side guarantee that generated ABAP passes through Format is not enforced. hir/abap EmitNamed, by contrast, does propagate the error. Not a regression, because drivers were never wrapped before.

Full-line '*' comments and lines that start inside string-template text longer than 255 bytes make Format fail with 'unbreakable source line'. The old wrap would have split them, which corrupts semantics anyway, so failing is arguably better; it is just a behaviour change worth knowing about.
